venue.name: Horne Lake Cave Tours and Outdoor Centre
venue.description: Horne Lake Caves Provincial Park sits in the Beaufort Range about 30 minutes west of Qualicum Beach, and guided caving tours run from a visitor centre there all year. Every tour starts with a 1km moderately strenuous uphill hike to the cave entrance. The caves are wild, with no lighting, paved walkways or handrails, and each tour sets its own youngest age. Schools, home learners and verified non profit groups get a reduced mid-week rate on two of the tours.
venue.address: 3905 Horne Lake Caves Rd Qualicum Beach, BC V9K 2L7

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Our caves are wild and natural, with no lighting, paved walkways, or hand-railings.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: All tours begin with a 1km moderately strenuous uphill hike, which is broken up with 7 informative stops.
facility_notes.rain_backup: Tours proceed as scheduled regardless of weather conditions.

venue.nearby_park: The neighbouring Horne Lake Regional Park Campground has hiking, canoe rentals, beach walking and bird watching.
restrictions: No backpacks in the cave, but small hip pouches or fanny packs are fine
NO flip-flops, sandals, or holey soles permitted
Children 5-15 years old must be accompanied by an adult
Dogs and other pets are not permitted inside any of the caves
All park visitors entering the caves must clean their shoes to remove White Nose Syndrome spores
No personal caving equipment that has been into any caves off of Vancouver Island
Please do not apply perfume or after-shave, because the enclosed spaces make it difficult for those with scent sensitivities
Adult participants aged 19 and over sign a liability waiver, and every participant under 19 needs a signed parental consent and medical form
venue.seasonal_notes: Cave tours run all year and the caves stay at 8 degrees Celsius whatever the season. Summer and Fall are driest with tours departing every day, and in Winter and Spring you are asked to call ahead. Horne Lake Road is a 12km gravel road shared with logging trucks, and snow between January and March can postpone tours until it is plowed.

programs.name: School group tour, One Cave (Riverbend Cave)
programs.description: A private guided trip into Riverbend Cave for school and home learning groups. A 1km uphill hike through karst rainforest, led by a naturalist cave guide, covers the geological processes, rock types, fossils, calcite crystals and local plants and animals before the group goes underground. Riverbend is the easiest of the caves and is designed to avoid crawling or squeezing. The $35 rate is for verified non profit organisations and only applies Monday to Friday. The same tour is $59 per person at the regular public rate. From October to April the youngest age for a school group rises to 8.
programs.what_children_do: Walk about a kilometre uphill through forest, stopping seven times along the way to look at rock and talk about how the caves formed. Then, in helmets with headlamps, follow a guide into an unlit cave, crouching and using their hands to balance over river rocks while looking at fossils and crystal formations.
programs.our_note: Getting there is part of the trip. The last stretch is 12km of gravel logging road, so add time and talk to your driver first. Everyone needs closed shoes and warm layers, because the cave sits at 8 degrees all year and rubber boots are the better choice from October to April.
programs.practical_summary: The visit is a hike plus a wild cave, so it is not step-free and a stroller will not go. Washrooms, indoor lunch space and bus parking are not mentioned anywhere on the site, so those are worth a call before you commit.
programs.extra_fees_note: Their booking software adds a 3% processing fee per booking, and non profit organisations are exempt from it.
programs.payment_timing: A 50% deposit is made by payment authorization form to hold the booking, and the group is invoiced for the numbers given up to 24 hours before arrival.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations are accepted by email only. There are no refunds for changes or cancellations within 24 hours of departure, none for no-shows, and the group deposit is not refundable.

chaperone_ratio.applies_to: sub groups of up to 15 youth and adults combined, one supervising adult each

programs.name: School group tour, Multi-Cave Explorer
programs.description: A private guided trip for school and home learning groups that does Riverbend Cave first, then takes a short hike to Main Cave for more adventurous caving. Main Cave has a narrow standing entrance squeeze, ladders, a three tier waterfall climb with no ropes, and Canada's only cave slide. The site gives the duration as 2.5 to 3 hours. The $35 rate is for verified non profit organisations and only applies Monday to Friday. The same tour is $84 per person at the regular public rate.
programs.what_children_do: Hike a kilometre uphill, then go through two caves in helmets and headlamps. In Main Cave they side-step through a standing squeeze, climb up and down ladders, walk crouched low, scramble up a three tier waterfall and slide down a cave slide.
programs.our_note: This is the physical one. Expect three hours of climbing, squeezing and getting wet, so it suits a group that is already used to a long active day. Ask about a private tour if you have anyone between 5 and 8, because that is the only way the site says younger children can come.
programs.practical_summary: Long, wet and underground, with a hike at either end and no step-free route. Washrooms, indoor lunch space and bus parking are not stated on the site, so ask about all three when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: Their booking software adds a 3% processing fee per booking, and non profit organisations are exempt from it.
programs.payment_timing: A 50% deposit is made by payment authorization form to hold the booking, and the group is invoiced for the numbers given up to 24 hours before arrival.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations are accepted by email only. There are no refunds for changes or cancellations within 24 hours of departure, none for no-shows, and the group deposit is not refundable.

programs.name: The Action Pack (Main & Lower Caves)
programs.description: A guided trip into two obstacle based caves a seven minute hike from the visitor centre, with short squeezes and climbs, calcite formations and fossils. This is a regular public tour rather than a school offering, so the price is the public one. Groups of ten or more can contact the groups coordinator for custom tour times and 15% off regular prices.
programs.what_children_do: Hike about seven minutes from the visitor centre, then in helmets and headlamps work through two wild caves, squeezing through short narrow sections and climbing over rock with a guide close by.
programs.our_note: Shorter and closer in than the school tours, which makes it the easiest one to fit around a bus schedule. There is no school rate on it, so ask the groups coordinator about the discount for ten or more before you compare costs.
programs.practical_summary: A short walk and two wild caves, with no step-free route and no seating. Washrooms, lunch space and bus parking are not stated on the site, so check when you call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Their booking software adds a 3% processing fee per booking, and non profit organisations are exempt from it.
programs.payment_timing: Reservations for cave tours must be paid in full at time of booking.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations are accepted by email only, and there are no refunds for changes or cancellations within 24 hours of departure.

programs.name: Achilles Challenge
programs.description: A vertical caving trip beyond the crawlways in Riverbend Cave, with three belly crawls, a 6m rock climb and a 5m cable ladder climb. Kneepads are provided and no previous rope experience is needed. The site says it is only available June to September. This is a regular public tour rather than a school offering. Groups of ten or more can contact the groups coordinator for custom tour times and 15% off regular prices.
programs.what_children_do: Hike a kilometre uphill, then crawl on hands and knees and on their bellies through passages as low as 18 inches, climb rock and a cable ladder, and clip into a handline to traverse a rock shelf above a large calcite formation.
programs.our_note: This one is set at 13 and up, so it is a secondary school trip rather than an elementary one. Four hours underground with crawls that tight is a lot to ask of a first time caver, and the tightest crawl is about 18 inches high.
programs.practical_summary: Four hours of hard physical caving with crawls, climbs and ladders, available in summer only. Washrooms, lunch space and bus parking are not stated on the site, so ask when you call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Their booking software adds a 3% processing fee per booking, and non profit organisations are exempt from it.
programs.payment_timing: Reservations for cave tours must be paid in full at time of booking.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations are accepted by email only, and there are no refunds for changes or cancellations within 24 hours of departure.

programs.name: Max Depth Adventure
programs.description: The longest trip on offer, running the full length of Riverbend Cave past Achilles Pot to the deepest reaches, with crawlways, climbs and rappels of up to 20m. The 5.5 hours include a 30 minute above ground rappel practice before going in. The site says it is only available May to September. This is a regular public tour rather than a school offering. Groups of ten or more can contact the groups coordinator for custom tour times and 15% off regular prices.
programs.what_children_do: Practise rappelling above ground for half an hour, then spend more than four hours underground crawling, climbing a 10.5m rock pitch and a 10m vertical ladder, and rappelling into a seven storey chamber.
programs.our_note: Set at 13 and up and built for teenagers with stamina. Harness sizing is a real limit here, so check the waist and thigh measurements against your group before you promise anyone a place.
programs.practical_summary: Five and a half hours of technical caving with rappels and long climbs, in summer only. Washrooms, lunch space and bus parking are not stated on the site, so ask when you call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Their booking software adds a 3% processing fee per booking, and non profit organisations are exempt from it.
programs.payment_timing: Reservations for cave tours must be paid in full at time of booking.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations are accepted by email only, and there are no refunds for changes or cancellations within 24 hours of departure.

gaps: Washrooms are never mentioned on the site. There is a visitor centre, but nothing says what is in it, so ask before you go.
Indoor lunch space is not mentioned. The visitor centre has a museum display and short videos, but nothing says a group can eat there.
Nothing says where a school bus parks or whether it can turn around, which matters because the last 12km is a gravel logging road shared with logging trucks.
No start times are published. You request a departure time on the registration form and they quote you back, so the day cannot be planned from the site alone.
The $35 group rate carries no date or season anywhere on the site, so confirm it is still current when you book.
The site does not say how many guides come with a large group or how a class of 42 is split on the day, only that extra guides can be arranged.
The two week deadline for confirming numbers comes from their group leader checklist rather than from a booking page, so treat it as their working deadline.
The youngest age of 6 for the Riverbend school tour is taken from that same tour's public listing on the home page. The school page itself only states the October to April minimum of 8.

How many adults have to come is written as sub groups of up to 15 youth and adults combined with one supervising adult each, rather than as a plain number of children per adult, so the exact ratio is worth confirming.
Nothing on the site addresses whether the tours suit children who find noise, darkness or close spaces hard, beyond a general note that nervousness is normal.
There is a self guided option in the open access caves with helmet and light rental at $6 plus tax, but no group rate is published for it.
Every photograph on the site uses its file name in place of alt text, so the image descriptions here were written after opening and looking at each picture.
The map link in the site footer carries only a map centre, not a place pin, so the coordinates here were geocoded from the visitor centre and then checked against that centre.

conflicts.note: Two different numbers are given for their visitor centre. The school page lists one and the rest of the site lists another. Try the one on their contact page first and use the other if nobody picks up.
Their own group pages give two different addresses for confirming your numbers, one starting groups and one starting education. If one bounces, try the other.
